reason: The page suspends the June 19, 1912 eight-hour statute for three broad military-contract categories during the pending emergency and until further orders. Neither the emergency reference nor the absence of named later actors proves a first ending date.

The page excepts labor on one proposed Assay Office building from the eight-hour limit, effective from its signing date. It has no fixed sunset; the project purpose does not prove when construction ended.

The page declares the specified water mains an emergency construction measure, excepts associated labor from the eight-hour law, and preserves time-and-a-half overtime pay. The quoted fiscal-year appropriation period does not itself date the work or end the exception.
The page excepts labor on proposed New York Marine Hospital structures, effective from the signing date. Completion is a plausible end but no held occurrence evidence dates it.

The page authorizes the Public Printer to appoint skilled laborers without civil-service requirements during the war and says it will be revoked when necessity passes. This authorizes appointments, not proof that any happened or that revocation occurred; EO 3461 remains a truncated, uninspected actor lead.
The order excuses work on Friday March 4 1921 only; the proviso limits that same day. It has no operative command on March 5.
